questions.q: Under marine insurance, the principle that the insured must stand to suffer a financial loss if the insured property is damaged is known as...
questions.explanation: Insurable interest requires the insured to have a financial stake in the subject matter so that a loss would affect the insured. Indemnity concerns restoring the insured to the pre-loss financial position, while subrogation and contribution apply after a claim has been paid.

questions.q: A policy that provides protection for a fixed period and pays the sum assured only if the insured dies within that period is called...
questions.explanation: Term assurance covers the insured for a specified number of years and pays a death benefit only if death occurs during the term. Whole life assurance runs for the whole of life, while an endowment assurance also pays on survival to the maturity date.

questions.q: Yemi's comprehensive motor policy has an excess of ₦50,000. After a covered accident, the repair cost is ₦180,000. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: The policy excess is the first part of the loss that the insured bears, so the insurer pays ₦180,000 − ₦50,000 = ₦130,000. Paying ₦180,000 would ignore the excess, while ₦50,000 is the insured's own share, not the insurer's payment.

questions.q: A number of independent retailers pool their funds to buy goods in large quantities from manufacturers and then share the goods according to their purchases. This organization is a...
questions.explanation: A retail cooperative society is owned by its members, who combine their buying power to obtain goods in bulk and share them according to their purchases. A department store and a multiple shop are single business organizations, while a mail-order firm mainly sells through orders rather than pooled buying.

questions.q: Which service is a wholesaler most likely to render to a manufacturer?
options: Providing information about consumers' preferences and market trends
Selling goods in small quantities to final consumers
Granting unsecured loans to final consumers
questions.explanation: A wholesaler links manufacturers with retailers and can pass back useful market information about demand, consumer taste and price trends. Selling in small quantities to final consumers is normally a retailer's function, and unsecured loans to final consumers are not a standard wholesale service.

questions.q: Ahmed obtains a bank overdraft of ₦250,000 at 12% simple interest per annum for 4 months. How much interest will he pay?
questions.explanation: Interest is calculated as principal × rate × time = ₦250,000 × 12% × 4/12 = ₦10,000. Using 12 months instead of 4 months gives ₦30,000, which is the full-year interest, not the interest for four months.

questions.q: The market for short-term funds and instruments such as treasury bills, commercial papers and certificates of deposit is called the...
questions.explanation: The money market deals in short-term funds and near-money instruments such as treasury bills, commercial papers and certificates of deposit. The capital market handles long-term funds, while the foreign exchange market deals in currencies.

questions.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of a consumer rather than a consumer right?
options: Receiving a replacement for defective goods
Checking the condition and expiry date of goods before buying them
questions.explanation: A consumer is expected to take reasonable care by inspecting goods and checking expiry dates before purchase. Receiving replacements, protection from false advertising and seeking redress are rights protected under consumer protection rules.

questions.q: A market union in Aba refuses to allow customers to return defective goods, even when the defect was present at the time of sale. Which consumer right is being denied?
options: The right to satisfaction of basic needs
questions.explanation: The right to redress entitles a consumer to a remedy, such as repair, replacement or refund, when goods are defective. Refusing returns for defects present at the time of sale denies this right rather than the right to choose or to be educated.

questions.q: When a seller discovers that a customer was overcharged on an invoice, the document sent to correct the overcharge is a
questions.explanation: A credit note is sent to inform the buyer that the seller's account has been credited in respect of an overcharge or returned goods. A debit note is used to increase the amount owed, while a pro forma invoice is a quotation sent before a sale. A consular invoice is certified by a consular officer for export purposes.

questions.q: An exporter in Apapa presents shipping documents to a bank which, on behalf of the buyer, has promised to pay when the documents are in order. The document containing this promise is a
questions.explanation: A letter of credit is issued by the buyer's bank and constitutes an undertaking to pay the exporter when the specified shipping documents are presented and found to be in order. A bill of lading is a carrier's receipt and contract of carriage, not a bank's promise to pay. A certificate of origin and a packing list support the shipment but do not themselves undertake payment.

questions.q: Chief Nwosu imports goods and stores them in a bonded warehouse before customs duty is paid. To transfer the right to collect the goods to a buyer while they remain in the warehouse, he should endorse a
questions.explanation: A warehouse warrant is a transferable receipt and document of title for goods stored in a bonded warehouse, and it may be endorsed to transfer the right to the goods. A delivery note accompanies goods and shows that they have been delivered, while a bill of exchange is an order to pay money. A mate's receipt is a temporary receipt issued by a ship's officer for goods received on board.

questions.q: An online store in Lagos uses a service that keeps a buyer's payment with a neutral third party until the buyer confirms that the goods have been received as described. This service is called
questions.explanation: An escrow service holds the buyer's money with a neutral third party and releases it to the seller only after the buyer confirms satisfactory receipt of the goods. A shopping cart is merely a feature for selecting goods before checkout. A chargeback is a reversal of a card payment, while electronic data interchange is the computer-to-computer exchange of business documents.

questions.q: A company in Port Harcourt wishes to move crude oil continuously overland to a refinery in Warri without loading it into individual containers. The most suitable mode of transport is
questions.explanation: A pipeline is suitable for moving liquids such as crude oil continuously over long distances and generally has low operating costs once installed. Road tankers and rail tank wagons require the liquid to be loaded into individual vehicles and moved in batches. Air cargo is very costly and unsuitable for large quantities of crude oil.

questions.q: A bank with branches in Abuja, Kano and Port Harcourt wants to hold a live interactive meeting of its managers without any of them travelling. The most suitable service is
questions.explanation: Videoconferencing allows people in different locations to see and hear one another and to discuss matters live without travelling. Telex and registered mail are written message services and do not permit live interaction. A courier service moves physical items and would cause delay.

questions.q: A newly opened small bakery in Abeokuta wants to promote its daily bread prices to residents within the town at low cost. The most suitable advertising medium is
questions.explanation: Local radio can reach residents within the town at relatively low cost and allows frequent, timely announcements of daily prices. National television and international magazines are costly and reach audiences far beyond the bakery's local market. A highway billboard is less suitable for frequently changing daily price information.

questions.q: Many customers of a soap company in Ilorin continue to buy its brand without comparing it with competitors because they have used it for years. This behaviour is best described as
questions.explanation: Brand loyalty is the tendency of customers to keep buying a particular brand repeatedly because of satisfaction or familiarity. Market segmentation is the division of a market into groups of buyers, while product differentiation is the process of making a product appear distinct from competing products. Sales promotion refers to short-term incentives such as discounts or free samples.

questions.q: A partnership in which all the partners have unlimited liability and may take an active part in the management of the business is known as...
questions.explanation: In an ordinary partnership, every partner has unlimited liability and may be involved in management. A limited partnership has at least one partner whose liability is limited and who does not manage the firm, while a private limited liability company and a cooperative society are separate forms of business organisation.

questions.q: Public corporations in Nigeria are usually established by...
options: registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission
a partnership deed signed by members
a resolution of a cooperative society
a law passed by the legislature
questions.explanation: Public corporations are created by statute, such as an Act of the National Assembly or a state law, to perform specified public functions. Registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission is used for companies, while a partnership deed and cooperative resolution do not create a public corporation.

questions.q: Adebayo buys 500 shares of a quoted company from another investor through the Nigerian Exchange. The company that issued the shares receives no money from this transaction. Adebayo has bought the shares in the...
questions.explanation: The secondary market is where existing securities are traded among investors, so the company does not receive new capital. The primary market is where new securities are issued to raise fresh funds for the company.

questions.q: A manufacturing company in Lagos wants to obtain long-term capital by offering its shares to the public for the first time through the Nigerian Exchange. This offer is known as...
questions.explanation: An initial public offering is the first sale of shares by a company to the general public, and it raises long-term capital for the company. A rights issue offers additional shares to existing shareholders, a secondary market transaction involves existing shares, and a share transfer only changes the holder of existing shares.

questions.q: A Lagos importer asks his bank to issue a letter of credit in favour of a supplier in China. Under the letter of credit, the document the Chinese supplier usually draws on the bank to demand payment is a...
questions.explanation: In a letter of credit transaction, the exporter usually draws a bill of exchange on the bank named in the credit to demand payment. A bill of lading is a transport document, while a certificate of origin and an import licence serve regulatory purposes.

questions.q: ECOWAS member countries apply a common external tariff on goods imported from countries outside ECOWAS. This arrangement is mainly intended to...
options: tax locally manufactured goods sold within a member country
remove all duties on goods traded within ECOWAS
protect community industries and harmonise tariffs against non-member countries
prevent member countries from exporting to Europe
questions.explanation: The common external tariff applies to imports from outside ECOWAS, helping to protect industries within the community and standardise tariff treatment of non-member countries. It is not a tax on goods produced and sold locally, and duties on goods traded within ECOWAS are handled under the region's free trade arrangement rather than the external tariff.

questions.q: The work of a legal practitioner in Abuja who gives legal advice and represents clients in court belongs to which occupational group?
questions.explanation: Legal advice and representation are services, which place the legal practitioner in the tertiary occupational group. Primary occupations involve extraction from nature, secondary occupations involve manufacturing or processing, and extractive occupations are a branch of primary occupations.

questions.q: The difference between the total value of a firm's output and the cost of intermediate goods purchased from other firms is known as...
questions.explanation: Value added measures the firm's contribution to production after subtracting the cost of intermediate inputs from the value of output. Gross profit and total revenue are not defined in this way, while net national product is a macroeconomic aggregate.

questions.q: Bola insured her boutique stock against fire for ₦2,000,000. The policy had a ₦50,000 excess clause, and no average clause applied. Fire destroyed stock valued at ₦700,000. What amount is the insurer expected to pay?
questions.explanation: The insurer pays the actual loss less the excess: ₦700,000 − ₦50,000 = ₦650,000. The sum insured is the maximum cover, not the amount automatically paid for a smaller loss.

questions.q: Kunle paid ₦24,000 for a one-year motor insurance policy starting on 1 March. He sold the car on 31 August and the insurer agreed to refund the unused premium on a pro-rata basis. How much refund is due?
questions.explanation: The policy was used for six months, March to August, leaving six months unused out of twelve. The refund is 6/12 × ₦24,000 = ₦12,000.

questions.q: Teachers in Kaduna formed an association, contributed capital, and bought rice and cooking oil in bulk to sell to members at fair prices. The retail organization described is a
questions.explanation: A consumer co-operative society is owned by its members and buys goods in bulk to resell to members at fair prices, sharing any surplus. A private limited company is investor-owned, while a departmental store and multiple shop are other forms of large-scale retailing.

questions.q: What is a major advantage of mail-order retailing over a small open shop?
options: It gives every customer unlimited credit.
Delivery is always faster than buying in a shop.
Customers can inspect the goods physically before paying.
It can serve customers in distant places without a costly shop front.
questions.explanation: Mail-order retailing uses catalogues or online ordering and delivery, so it can reach customers far beyond a local shop without expensive shop premises. Physical inspection and immediate delivery are usually disadvantages of mail order, and unlimited credit is not a normal feature.

questions.q: Ngozi, a retailer in Aba, received cartons of soap worth ₦85,000 from a wholesaler. On checking, goods valued at ₦7,000 were damaged and returned. Which document should the wholesaler issue to adjust Ngozi's account?
questions.explanation: A credit note is issued by a seller when goods are returned or an allowance is granted, reducing the buyer's indebtedness. A debit note normally charges the other party, while an invoice demands payment and a consignment note covers goods sent on consignment.

questions.q: A civil servant in Abuja instructs his bank to pay ₦25,000 from his account to his landlord on the first day of every month. The instruction is best described as a
questions.explanation: A standing order is a fixed instruction to a bank to make regular payments of a stated amount. A bank draft is a cheque-like instrument bought from a bank, while a letter of credit supports trade payment and a promissory note is a written promise to pay.

questions.q: Which institution insures deposits in licensed banks in Nigeria in order to protect depositors in the event of a bank failure?
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation administers deposit insurance for licensed banks and related institutions and pays insured depositors up to the prescribed limit if a bank fails. The Central Bank regulates banks but does not run deposit insurance, while the Securities and Exchange Commission regulates securities and the National Insurance Commission supervises insurers.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a consumer's right to redress?
options: The right to choose freely among competing products.
The right to receive sufficient information about products before buying them.
The right to obtain compensation or correction when goods or services cause harm or fail to meet agreed terms.
The right to be protected against goods that are unsafe.
questions.explanation: Redress concerns remedies such as refund, replacement or compensation after a wrong has occurred. Information, choice and safety are separate consumer rights, although they may also apply before or during a purchase.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter of cocoa beans to Europe is required to present a document showing the country where the cocoa was produced in order to qualify for preferential import duty. Which document should the exporter present?
questions.explanation: A certificate of origin states the country in which the goods were produced or manufactured, which customs authorities use to determine preferential duty treatment. A bill of lading mainly evidences the contract of carriage, while a marine insurance certificate covers loss or damage to the goods in transit.

questions.q: A clearing agent at Apapa needs a document showing how goods are packed, the marks on each package and the number of cartons, but not their prices. Which document is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A packing list shows the manner of packing, marks, number of packages and related details without stating the prices of the goods. A commercial invoice shows values, while a bill of lading is chiefly evidence of the contract of carriage.

questions.q: A payment platform in Lagos allows an online merchant to accept card payments without the merchant seeing the customer's full card details. Which e-commerce facility performs this function?
questions.explanation: A payment gateway securely authorises and processes card payments between the customer, the merchant and the payment processor. A shopping cart only lets a customer select goods, while electronic data interchange is used for exchanging business documents between organisations.

questions.q: A consignee in Lagos receives a notice from the shipping line that a container has arrived at Apapa port and is ready for clearance. What is this notice called?
questions.explanation: An arrival notice informs the consignee or agent that the goods have arrived and are ready for clearing. A ship's manifest lists all cargo on the vessel, while a bill of lading is evidence of the contract of carriage.

questions.q: A bank in Abuja wants to send a confidential scanned contract to its lawyer in Lagos immediately and keep a record of the exact document sent. Which channel is most suitable?
options: Electronic mail with a scanned attachment
questions.explanation: Electronic mail can transmit a scanned copy of a document immediately and keep a record in the sender's mailbox. A telephone call cannot send a scanned document, while ordinary post and telegraph do not provide immediate transmission of the exact copy.

questions.q: A new rechargeable lamp is advertised by explaining how it works, its voltage and the warranty attached to it. Which type of advertising is being used?
questions.explanation: Informative advertising gives factual details about a product, especially when it is new, in order to create initial awareness and understanding. Persuasive advertising tries to make consumers prefer one brand over another, while reminder advertising keeps an established brand in consumers' minds.

questions.q: A trader in Kano selling a new soap takes it to markets, demonstrates its use and persuades buyers face to face. Which promotional method is being used?
questions.explanation: Personal selling involves direct face-to-face contact between a seller and a buyer to persuade the buyer to purchase. Advertising is paid non-personal communication, while publicity is unpaid mention of a business or product by the media.

questions.q: A small bakery in Abeokuta is unsure whether customers prefer wheat bread or coconut bread before introducing both. Which marketing activity should it carry out first?
questions.explanation: Marketing research gathers information about customers' needs and preferences before production or launching decisions are made. Market segmentation divides a market into groups, while sales promotion and product differentiation are used after the product offer has been developed.

questions.q: A company in Enugu is incorporated as a limited liability company. Which feature best shows that the company has a legal existence separate from its shareholders?
options: It ceases to exist whenever a shareholder dies.
It can own property and sue or be sued in its own name.
All its shareholders must be residents of Enugu State.
Its directors are personally liable for all the company's debts.
questions.explanation: Incorporation gives a company a separate legal personality, so it can own property and sue or be sued in its own name. Shareholders do not become personally liable for company debts merely because they own shares, and the death of a shareholder does not ordinarily end the company.

questions.q: In a cooperative society, control is normally exercised on the principle of
options: the size of each member's capital contribution.
the value of each member's annual purchases.
questions.explanation: A cooperative is democratically controlled, usually through the one-member-one-vote principle rather than the number of shares held. Distributing surplus according to purchases may occur as a rebate, but it does not determine voting control.

questions.q: An investor buys shares of a company quoted on the Nigerian Exchange when the shares are marked cum dividend. This means the investor will
options: lose the dividend to the seller of the shares.
pay a lower price because the dividend has already been paid.
receive the dividend already declared by the company.
receive only a bonus issue in place of the dividend.
questions.explanation: Cum dividend means the shares are traded together with the right to the declared dividend, so the buyer becomes entitled to it. A share sold after the ex-dividend date would not carry that dividend right.

questions.q: A market situation in which share prices are generally falling as investors expect poor corporate results is described as
questions.explanation: A bear market is characterised by falling share prices and pessimistic investor expectations. A bull market is the opposite, with generally rising prices, while the money market handles short-term funds.

questions.q: A stockbroker receives an instruction from a client to sell 500 shares on the Nigerian Exchange 'at best'. The broker should sell the shares
options: at the price at which the client originally bought them.
after waiting until a stated target price is reached.
at the best price obtainable in the market at that time.
only to another stockbroker on the trading floor.
questions.explanation: An 'at best' order is a market order, so the broker executes it at the most favourable price currently available. A target price would be relevant to a limit order, which is not what the client gave.

questions.q: The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and visible imports is called the
questions.explanation: The balance of trade compares visible exports with visible imports. The balance of payments is a broader record of all international transactions, including invisible items and capital flows.

questions.q: A firm that uses a large amount of machinery relative to labour in its production process is said to be
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive production relies more on machines and equipment than on human labour. Labour-intensive production would use a higher proportion of workers.

questions.q: Which of the following is a capital good?
options: A delivery van bought by a supermarket for distributing goods.
A pair of shoes bought by a student for personal use.
A bag of rice bought by a family for household consumption.
A loaf of bread bought by a worker for breakfast.
questions.explanation: Capital goods are used by producers to produce other goods or services, such as a delivery van used in distribution. The bread, shoes and rice are consumer goods because they directly satisfy personal wants.

questions.q: The people in a country who are able and willing to work, whether employed or unemployed, make up the country's
questions.explanation: The labour force consists of persons who are able and willing to work, whether employed or unemployed. The dependent population consists mainly of persons too young or too old to work, while total population includes everyone.
